chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام.

Regarding a man who married his bondwoman to another man and stipulated for him that whatever child she gave birth to would be free; then her husband divorced her or died, so he married her to another man. What is the status of her child?

He عليه السلام said: 'The child is in her status. He only made that stipulation for the first one, and with respect to the latter he has the choice: if he wishes, he may emancipate, and if he wishes, he may retain.'

key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: having the legal option or choice
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَتِهَا: with the same legal status as her

ai.seo_question: If a bondwoman's owner stipulates that her children from one marriage are free, does that ruling also apply to children from a later husband?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about a bondwoman whose owner stipulated freedom for children born from her first marriage. The Imam عليه السلام states that the stipulation applies only to the first husband, and children from a later marriage follow the mother's status unless the owner chooses to emancipate them. It is significant for rulings on conditional emancipation, marriage of bondwomen, and the legal status of offspring.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3444 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a man who married his bondwoman to another man and stipulated that any child she bore would be free. Then her husband either divorced her or died, and she was married to another man.
I asked: "What is the status of her child in this case?"

Imam (as) said: "The child is regarded like her. That condition applied only to the first husband. As for the second husband, he has the option-if he wishes, he may free the child, and if he wishes, he may keep the child as a slave."
